vectors.name: clean-disjoint-pass
vectors.note: mutant and predicate authored by different, disjoint DECLARED identities; the gate's observed attribution matches A_i exactly -- PASS, and the declared-identity-inequality floor holds at its real (checkable) strength -- not git-verified repository attribution.

vectors.name: same-author-disjointness-violation
vectors.note: mutant and predicate authored by the SAME declared identity -- disjointness_holds is false (a real, mechanically-caught floor violation), reported as its own fact, separate from the conformance verdict (which still computes normally on its own inputs).

vectors.name: set-valued-attribution-order-independence
vectors.note: A_i is a declared canon.set.v0 (member order not semantic). The gate's observed set is the SAME members in a DIFFERENT order -- canonical(A_i) must still match, so this is PASS, proving the sort-then-JCS fix actually normalizes order (a naive per-array JCS would wrongly report CONFORMANCE_FAILED here).

vectors.name: declared-set-with-duplicate-is-rejected-not-deduped
vectors.note: A_i is declared canon.set.v0 but its own value carries a duplicate member -- MALFORMED, fails closed as UNRESOLVED/malformed_predicate (the PREDICATE side, since A_i itself is the malformed one). The obvious first draft silently dedupes a duplicate-bearing 'set', which hides the exact defect (whoever fed this isn't actually emitting a set) the same way folding distinct causes into one marker string does. A gate that dedupes here would wrongly report a verdict at all.

vectors.name: canon-mismatch-same-value-different-declared-canon
vectors.note: The SAME array value ['integer_overflow','reentrancy'] (already duplicate-free and already JCS-byte-sorted, so canon.set.v0's own sort is a no-op here) is declared canon.set.v0 in A_i and canon.sequence.v0 in observed_attribution -- literally identical canonicalValue either way, yet the verdict is CONFORMANCE_FAILED because canon_id sits inside the hash preimage. A gate that hashed only the canonicalized value (dropping canon_id from the preimage) would wrongly PASS this vector.

vectors.name: unresolved-no-observation
vectors.note: The gate under test never produced an observation (crashed, timed out, or genuinely could not run) -- UNRESOLVED/no_observation, NOT silently treated as a pass, NOT collapsed into CONFORMANCE_FAILED (which would falsely claim a determinate disagreement that never happened).

vectors.name: conformance-failed-real-disagreement
vectors.note: The gate under test genuinely disagrees with A_i (both exist, both determinate, both differ) -- CONFORMANCE_FAILED, the honest determinate-disagreement state, distinct from UNRESOLVED.

vectors.name: repair-run-restores-pass
vectors.note: The original run mismatched (CONFORMANCE_FAILED); a repair to the mutant is applied and RE-RUN through the SAME bound-run path (a bound recomputing run per C5, not a stored boolean) -- the repair-run's own observed_attribution now matches A_i, so repair_verdict is PASS while the ORIGINAL conformance_verdict on this vector stays whatever it genuinely was.

vectors.name: malformed-observation-well-formed-predicate
vectors.note: FIXED 2026-08-18 (Pavlo, PR #14 review): A_i is well-formed (canon.set.v0, no duplicates) but the OBSERVED attribution is the malformed one (duplicate-bearing). Prior code returned malformed_predicate for both a malformed predicate AND a malformed observed attribution, the exact collapsed-marker defect this thread's own rule exists to catch -- now UNRESOLVED/malformed_observation, a distinct reason for the observation-side failure.

vectors.name: canon-scalar-rejects-array-value
vectors.note: FIXED 2026-08-18 (Pavlo, PR #14 review): A_i declares canon.scalar.v0 but hands an array value -- the spec always said non-array, but the implementation previously fell through and silently accepted it. Now rejected as UNRESOLVED/malformed_predicate, same fail-closed discipline as set.v0/sequence.v0's own shape checks.

vectors.name: precommit-not-consumed-stale-binding
vectors.note: FIXED 2026-08-18 (Pavlo, PR #14 review: 'the run objects are specified but not mechanically exercised'). A_i and observed_attribution are both well-formed and WOULD match -- but the run's own consumes_precommit is deliberately bound to a different (wrong) hash, not the one just recomputed from this precommit. The binding check fires BEFORE the attribution comparison ever runs: UNRESOLVED/precommit_not_consumed, proving a run that isn't correctly bound to its precommit cannot produce a meaningful verdict even when the underlying attributions would otherwise agree.

description: Recomputes a PIN-RECORD flow (precommit -> conformance-run -> optional repair-run) from raw inputs: declared-identity disjointness (C2, a checkable floor over the vector-supplied author_identity strings -- proves the two DECLARED strings differ, NOT git-resolved repository attribution; a real authorship check needs the same real-repo CI step C1 is deferred to), precommit_hash as sha256(JCS(the whole predicate-precommit.v0 record)) (C3, closes the delimiter-free-concatenation collision surface -- naive sha256(hash_a + hash_b + hash_c + variable_length_commit_id) is ambiguous at variable-length boundaries, and --tamper genuinely exercises that exact boundary by including oracle_author_commit in its concatenation), declared+versioned attribution canonicalization (A_i carries its own canon_id -- canon.set.v0/canon.sequence.v0/canon.scalar.v0 -- which is itself part of the hash preimage; canon.set.v0 REJECTS a duplicate-bearing value as malformed rather than silently deduping it; canon.scalar.v0 REJECTS an array value rather than silently accepting it; canon_id is really part of the hash preimage, not just documentation alongside it: an identical value declared under two different canon_ids mismatches by hash even though its canonicalized form is the same either way), a real bound predicate-conformance-run.v0/predicate-repair-run.v0 object whose consumes_precommit field is checked against the freshly recomputed precommit_hash BEFORE any attribution comparison happens (a run that is not correctly bound to the precommit it claims to consume cannot produce a meaningful verdict -- reason precommit_not_consumed), and a verdict enum {PASS, CONFORMANCE_FAILED, UNRESOLVED} where disagreement, inability-to-determine, a malformed PREDICATE attribution, and a malformed OBSERVED attribution are four distinct terminal states with no merge path (malformed_predicate and malformed_observation are never collapsed into one reason). Repair is a bound recomputing run (C5), never a stored boolean. Deliberately out of scope: C1 (git ancestry of precommit-introducing-commit before run_identity, AND resolving author_commit to a real git author) -- facts about repository history a vectors-based gate cannot check, belong in a real CI step against a real repo.
recompute: disjointness_holds = mutant.author_identity != predicate.oracle_author_identity (declared strings, not git-resolved) ; precommit_hash = sha256(JCS(predicate-precommit.v0 record)), null if the declared attribution is malformed ; a conformance/repair run is a bound object whose consumes_precommit MUST equal the freshly recomputed precommit_hash or the verdict is UNRESOLVED/precommit_not_consumed ; verdict = PASS if canonicalize(A_i)==canonicalize(observed), CONFORMANCE_FAILED if both well-formed and differ, UNRESOLVED (with reason -- no_predicate/malformed_predicate/no_observation/malformed_observation/precommit_not_consumed/other) otherwise
